**PR-8. The presentation contract every visual system inherits.** A visual system — Lighting, Trails, Instruments, HUD, the Filter, the rig animator, the `CameraSolver`'s host node — is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (CR-10) and:

1. subscribes as `PRESENTATION` (or `INPUT_SURFACE` if it also issues commands — the HUD's prompts do not; the chart table holds the class for VS-B and submits nothing at MVP, Chart Table CT-27 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus)*); the Debug Overlay alone is `DIAGNOSTIC`;
2. reads **last-committed** state through `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` read views; nodes the Perception Filter's tag contract marks *corruptible* obtain their displayed value from the Filter, truth-channel nodes read `SIM` directly, and the Debug Overlay reads the true channel for everything — which nodes default to which is the Filter GDD's to set (CR-10's two channels);
3. treats a notification as a dirty mark and does its reading and drawing in the render callback (the pipeline root's `frame_pre_draw` handler, C2 `[UNV]`) — never inside the notification handler, where writes are disabled and a long handler stalls P5 for every other subscriber;
4. writes **only** `CanvasItem`, `Material`, `Light2D`, particle and audio properties (8.11's manifest rule); never a block, never a command (render presentation has no submit API — CR-14 H4), never a physics body (that is a `PROJECTOR`); **never a camera or viewport property unless it is the pipeline root or the camera host** (C1);
5. interpolates every moving value with the kernel's `tick_alpha` and the read view's previous/current pair (D.3), then floors to base px in the body frame (PR-4 rules 2–3) — **one interpolator** (PR-4 rule 8);
6. animates on `present_time` (PR-9), never on wall-clock and never counts ticks; it may read the committed `T` and `tick_alpha` for clock-locked phases (the beacon's drawn aim; a hook-divisor presenter's interpolation alpha, PR-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* (a presentation that counts ticks would freeze under a render hitch while the world moved — the opposite of the honest hold D.3 wants);
7. **never causes a tick** (CR-11) and never blocks on one; if the state it needs has not been committed yet it draws the last committed state;
8. places every item at an integer base-px position in the body frame and declares its band (PR-5) — a node that sorts declares its sort origin as its floor-contact line, or its host face's if wall-mounted;
9. obeys the flash clamp of PR-13 for anything it animates in luminance.

Rationale: this is the renderer's copy of the concept's "corruption is presentation-only" rule, written so a lint can check it (8.11 routes the manifest rule to the lead programmer). *Alternative rejected:* letting presentation own small bits of state (a trail's fade timer, a gauge's needle lag) — the moment a trail's visibility depends on presentation state it is no longer the truth channel every hallucination is checked against (Failure & Trail's "pure reader" rule in the index). Camera state is one of the two presentation-owned states the pipeline admits, and C5 makes it non-persistent and reset on every cut so it can never diverge from the sim. **The other is the bounded exemption of registry `settle_response`** (In-World Instruments IW-11, K-2): a gauge needle's settle is closed-form in `present_time` from one `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` triple per instrument plus `prev_honest_pm`, drawn for HONEST readings only, never persisted or replicated and snapped on restore — it changes how a needle arrives, never what it settles to *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)*.

---

**PR-9. The presentation clock.** The pipeline owns `present_time`: a render-rate clock in seconds that advances by the render delta while the kernel is `RUNNING`, `SAVING` or `LOADING`-with-hold, is **frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`**, and is the only clock layer-0 presentation may animate on (flow scroll, dust, the fringe's 4–6 s breathing, the Filter's stage-2 wobble, and only the non-geometric phase of the beacon — its drawn aim is the kernel clock `beacon_aim(T)` with `tick_alpha`, Lighting's *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*). Horror rig stepping is the exception: the rig's pose is sim-driven (every 5th tick) and presentation interpolates nothing between steps (5.4: stepped playback is the look) — the segment pose is stepped and never tweened; only the record's *position* may be interpolated, with the five-tick alpha `alpha_5 = ((T_now − T_run) + tick_alpha) / HORROR_RUN_TICKS` that a presenter on a divisor-5 hook derives from the kernel's one-tick `tick_alpha` (Horror HE-F18, C-HE-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities)*. `present_time` reconciles three rules that otherwise collide: CR-16 ("`PAUSED` stops the tick but not rendering"), 7.4 ("the world simply stops, lit exactly as it was" — so the flow in the pipes must stop too, not just the sim) and CR-11 ("pausing presentation effects (reduced motion) never pauses the sim" — reduced motion scales *individual effects*, never `present_time`). Layers 3–4 run on the engine's process time, because the chart table must respond while paused; the HUD (layer 2) is frozen under pause with the world *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)*. **`SceneTree.paused` `[BIN]` is not the kernel's pause** (H10 — the kernel is scene-tree independent): the pipeline root maps game pause to kernel `PAUSED` via the control plane and applies the engine's `paused` to presentation nodes only if at all → ADR (tick driver). Under pause the world viewport may stop re-rendering (`render_target_update_mode` `[BIN]`, last frame held → ADR), which is also the `HIDDEN` state's behaviour; step 11 confirms no stale frame survives a resize. **A `RESCALING` (a window resize, a display change, a zoom press) while updates are disabled forces `UPDATE_ONCE` on the world viewport for the frame of change** and then restores `UPDATE_DISABLED`, so a paused resize never presents the reallocated viewport's black or stale buffer; the held frame is re-rendered at the new size from the same committed state (no sim tick, `present_time` still frozen) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

---

**PR-10. The Perception Filter hook point.** The pipeline provides exactly one full-screen hook: **a `ShaderMaterial` slot on the `SubViewportContainer`**, assigned and nulled only by the pipeline root — the Filter writes shader parameters only (registry `filter_route`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter)* — receiving the world viewport's output at screen resolution, drawn **below every `CanvasLayer`** — so the Filter pass **never samples or writes** the HUD, inspect card, menus, text chat, pings, letterbox bars or debug overlay (C-R; HR-1, HR-6, R-7 by construction). This is the fifth material of 8.10's "≤ 5 materials" row. Constraints on what the pass may do (ux-designer, adopted; the Filter GDD owns the effects): it **writes colour only** — no displacement, blur, chromatic aberration, pixelation or resolution change; it **only adds** violet or flesh at 4.4's places and never remaps sane hues, erodes shape or trail contrast, or drops hull below the measured floor; it obeys the flash clamp (PR-13); it never writes a camera or viewport property (C1). Its output is **multiplied by a truth-channel mask** — character sprites, hand tools, crewmate beams, trails, the true cone edge — **or decomposed into per-element materials** so truth-channel pixels are exact (C-R). Everything stage 2/3 does to the *whole image* goes in this slot; everything *per thing* — a lying gauge's gleam, a decoy light, a wholly substituted sprite (5.0) — goes on nodes inside layer 0 under PR-8: the Filter's own per-node materials; modifier state that Lighting reads (LO-18); and decoy overlays — Filter-owned lies that Lighting draws as unshaded sprites on light-mask bit 3 (LO-21, LO-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter and 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*. **The mask's production is → ADR**: (a) a second `SubViewport` sharing the camera pose that draws only truth-channel items as unlit silhouettes (cheap, no sort problem because it is a mask, not a composite), or (b) no mask, per-element materials only; the Filter GDD chooses — and has chosen (b) for MVP (`filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`: the container slot is `NOT_USED`, its material null by design; route (a) is a VS-A option only if the lighting spike proves an exact mask) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter)*. *Alternative rejected:* compositing truth-channel items in a second viewport **above** the filtered world — those items sort against corruptible ones on the same Y-sorted layer, and splitting a sorted layer across two viewports breaks PR-5. `BackBufferCopy` without the material slot is the engine alternative (8.10) → ADR.

---

**PR-11. Frame-rate independence.** The sim runs at 60 Hz (CR-1); the pipeline renders at whatever rate the display and settings allow and never changes the tick. **The acceptance test is the kernel's:** identical `state_hash` after a scripted 10-s input replay at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 (G3 + CR-11; spike step 13).

| Render rate | Ticks per frame | What presentation shows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 144 fps | 0 or 1 (ticks on ≈ 42 % of frames) | interpolated positions between the last two commits at `tick_alpha ∈ [0,1)`, floored: camera and sprites step one base px at the interpolated instant, **never twice in a frame (this holds for every f_render ≥ 60 Hz = the tick rate; below 60 a frame spans more than one tick and a 1 px/tick body steps 1 or 2 base px — the 40 and 30 fps rows) and never backward** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*; without interpolation 58 % of frames would repeat a pose | no sub-base-pixel motion exists at any fps unless the `1/k` quantum is adopted (C3); `L_render` shrinks to ≤ 6.9 ms, input latency is otherwise unchanged above 60 |
| 60 fps | 1 | with tick-before-render, `tick_alpha` at draw time is ≈ 0, so an **interpolated transform shows approximately the *previous* tick's position**: continuous motion carries **one tick (≈ 17 ms) of visual latency by construction**, because D.3 forbids extrapolation. **Discrete committed state** (a light toggled, a gauge value, a trail appearing) reads `current` and shows in the same frame — D.4's best case applies to it. Look-ahead reads the **raw** aim (C4) and so carries no tick | the design target; the latency is the price of the honest clamp and is the same at every fps |
| 30 fps | 2 (catch-up) | the latest commit; `tick_alpha` clamps at 1 after the second tick; motion shows every second tick's pose — 2-base-px steps for a 1 px/tick body, honest, not smoothed | input-to-pixel worst case 50 ms (D.4); acceptable; **the Deck floor under pass A** |
| 40 / 90 Hz (Deck panels) | 1.5 / 0.67 average | the interpolation path is what keeps motion even at rates that are not multiples of 60. At 90 Hz (0.67 ticks per frame) the step is 0 or +1 base px, the same promise as 144 fps. At 40 Hz (1.5 ticks per frame, ticks per frame alternating 2, 1) a 1 px/tick body steps +1, +2, +1, +2 base px per frame: whole base pixels, never fractional, never backward, honest and unsmoothed like the 30 fps row; the "never twice in a frame" promise does not apply below 60 fps *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)* | spike at 40 and 90 fps caps (step 13) |
| < 20 fps | up to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`, then sim-time lag (CR-17) | the latest commit; the world *slows* rather than extrapolates; a catch-up burst is ≤ 12 px and eases; only a named ≥ 48 px source (weld delta, Body shove, restore) triggers the camera cut (C5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the pipeline reports frame time to the Debug Overlay; never a visual compensation |

`tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 so a hitch holds the last pose rather than extrapolating (D.3's Pillar 1 argument). Presentation reads `delta` only to advance `present_time` and the solver's smoothing. **Tick driver → ADR** (engine-programmer): kernel D.4 assumes the physics callback drives the tick (`physics_ticks_per_second = 60`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame` (engine default 8; the kernel requires it set equal to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) `[BIN]` — if that caps catch-up `[UNV]`, the engine stops catching up below 15 fps) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from command-simulation-layer)*; kernel D.5 defines a kernel-side accumulator — two accumulators drift, one must be the clock. If the physics callback drives, **`physics_jitter_fix` is set to 0** (default 0.5 `[BIN]`) pending the spike, since a fixed-tick kernel that forbids wall-clock reads (H9) should not receive engine-smoothed steps; `delta_smoothing = true` `[BIN]` affects `_process` delta only `[UNV]` and is harmless. **Tick-before-render ordering** (`_physics_process` → `_process` in the same frame) is silent in `[REF]` and is step 13's check; D.4's best case for discrete state is conditional on it. **Position ownership tension with CR-4:** the kernel says movement "integrates on the physics side from the current intent so the sprite never waits a tick" — a position integrated outside the tick and drawn the same frame has no previous/current pair and no one-tick latency, which is a different interpolator from kernel-alpha. The tick-source ADR (kernel Open Q 2/3) must decide who owns position before "one interpolator" can mean kernel-only; until then both are described and neither is promised. **V-sync and caps (PR-14):** ship `VSYNC_ENABLED` (engine default `[BIN]`); expose `MAILBOX` as "uncapped, no tearing" and `DISABLED` + `max_fps` for benchmarking; never `ADAPTIVE` by default (behaviour on Windows D3D12 vs Vulkan NOT SOURCEABLE — the binary reports `driver.windows = vulkan` `[BIN]` while `[REF]` says D3D12 is the 4.6+ default; 8.12 step 1 prints the active driver and the GDD assumes neither).

---

**PR-12. HUD scale.** The HUD's integer scale is `H ∈ {H_default, …, 2·H_default}` with **`H_default = max(k, 3)`** — **never below 3× on any display** (registry: `HUD_MIN_SCALE` = 3) (C-R), player-raisable to 2× the default in integer steps (HR-12's 100–200 %), labelled in Settings **by resulting cap height in screen px** (e.g. "21 px / 28 px / 35 px / 42 px" at 1080p), not by percentage (ux-designer). At 1080p the steps are 3×–6×; on the Deck and at 720p **3×–6× over a 2× world**; the Settings screen offers only the steps where the HUD's `bottom_row_fit` holds (registry; `H_default` always — the fallback when `fit` is false; H 5 and 6 are not offered at a 1280-px picture until CF-HS-11 is resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*; at 1440p 4×–8×; at 2160p 6×–12×. H is **independent of k and of zoom** (8.1: "the frame grows, the world does not"). The reading face (7.1) scales continuously and is the only non-integer text in the game. **Reading-face rasterisation** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: reading-face text is rasterised by the font server at its **final screen pixel size** (the label's font size is set to `round(base_size · scale_pct · window_scale)` on a `Control` chain whose `CanvasLayer.scale` and `Control.scale` are `(1, 1)` and whose own size is in screen px), and is never drawn under an integer-scaled `CanvasLayer` (`scale = H`) or under the world container's scale, where the same glyphs would be bitmap-stretched and blur; the pixel-grid faces (HUD) keep the integer `H` path. How layers 3–4, which sit at root scale, receive screen-px sizes under each wiring is part of the wiring ADR `[UNV]`; the acceptance test is a screenshot at 100 %, 125 % and 200 % showing crisp glyph edges (manual). Consequences: (i) because the Deck ships at H = 3 over k = 2, **two integer scales in one window is an MVP requirement**, not a post-spike nicety — it is PR-7's wiring ADR; the engine-programmer's note that "the HUD's integer scale comes from the root stretch with `Control.scale = (1,1)`" holds only when H = k, and `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels = true` `[BIN]` stays on the root in every wiring; (ii) **7.0's critical-strip size cap (12 % × 5 % of frame) is exceeded by default on the Deck** at H = 3 over a 2× world (the plate is 1.5× larger relative to the picture than at 1080p) — routed to art-director as a known, accepted cost of C-R's 3× floor — **resolved by the HUD & Suit Layer GDD**: the cap is defined at the 1080p reference frame and the Deck overage is accepted; a letterbox hairline, if used, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)*; (iii) the arcminute floors per device class (desk monitor, TV, handheld) that justify the 3× floor are the accessibility-specialist's table — routed. HUD elements are anchor-relative to the picture (PR-2) and survive a fractional HUD canvas. **The mechanism** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: "anchors absorb the fraction" is not one, because a `Control`'s anchors resolve against the root viewport, not the picture; instead the pipeline root sizes a **HUD-root `Control` to `hud_rect / H`** (a possibly fractional size, at the HUD rect's origin, the HUD rect being pinned to the `k_base` picture, PR-2) on every `RESCALING`, and every HUD element anchors to that Control; `world_to_hud` (D.14) returns coordinates relative to it. `H_default = max(k_auto, 3)` (unchanged).

---

**PR-13. Photosensitivity and brightness.** The pipeline hosts the frame-level invariants; Lighting owns the per-light clamp through its modifier contract. (a) **Per light:** no light may produce more than **3 flashes per rolling 1-s window**, a flash being a pair of opposing luminance changes ≥ 10 %, red included (C-R); the alarm beacon's 2–3 s sweep (2.8) and the cryo lamp's gutter (0.3–0.5 s dips no more often than every 10–20 s, 2.2) pass; **the deployable's flicker (3.2) must be specified as a number and pass the clamp** — routed to art-director and technical-artist; the pipeline-side ceiling the art-director authors inside is at most 4 transitions per second (`F = 2`, one pair under `F_MAX`) at any amplitude ≥ 10 % (Open Question 6). **The clamp is analytic, not measured** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: Lighting computes each light's requested luminance transitions per tick from its modifier state (beacon sweep, cryo gutter, a deployable's flicker, a toggle), applies D.15's transition rule to that sequence and delays transitions *before* they are drawn; the regional and frame-mean sums use each light's luminance times its footprint in the region as an upper bound. A GPU readback is never in the clamp's path — it would either stall the frame or arrive frames late. (b) **Regional and frame-mean:** the same ceiling applies to each region of a 3 × 3 grid over the displayed picture at the current field (a ninth of it; 213 × 120 base px only at the default 640×360 field, 128 × 72 at the 384×216 field of `k_z` = 5 at 1080p — registry `flash_governor`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)* and to the frame mean, so overlapping lights cannot sum past it; **no full-frame flash in any state, on any layer** (7.3, HR-13). (c) **A "reduce flashing" toggle, separate from reduced motion**: deployables steady, power arcs held as glow, the beacon becomes a static mark + sound + HUD glyph (HR-8's form), the cryo gutter kept. **The toggle defaults ON on a fresh profile, at first launch** (default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): creative-director recommendation, design-review decision D79 / X10; a player who wants the full effects turns it off in settings); reduced motion keeps its default OFF. While it is on, the strict ceiling of (g) applies to every source with no exemptions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (d) **No full-frame gamma or brightness**; HR-15's bounded hull-material step is the only brightness control (PR-3 b). (e) A **first-launch photosensitivity notice** (chart-table register); it states that reduce flashing is already on and where to change it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (f) A **flash scan** of the 2.8 breach composition and the 2.4 lost state is a spike step (routed to the technical-artist's 8.12 list); the scan — a 3 × 3 region and frame-mean luminance reduction of the displayed picture, read back asynchronously so it is at least two frames late — is **verification only**, in dev builds and the flash-scan tool, absent from release builds, and costs at most 0.5 ms of GPU time on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (pending spike measurement; Open Question 20, closed by R12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*. > **Amendments from Section D (adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; these supersede any conflicting value stated above in Core Rules):** (1) the pan-speed ceiling is `1.25 × v_max` (not 1.25 × walk) and the lag cut `LAG_CUT` is **48 px**, not 24 — under first-order follow the steady-state lag is exactly `v·τ` and the camera's steady speed equals the avatar's, so a ceiling below `v_max` is unreachable by a legal follow of a runner and a 24 px cut would fire continuously at run speed; build invariant `LAG_CUT > v_max · τ_follow`. (2) The cut predicates evaluate the **follow component only**; look-ahead has its own slew clamp `L_SLEW_MAX = 144 px/s`, so a 180° aim flick does not trigger a cut (full reversal reaches 95 % in ≈ 1.4 s). (3) Look-ahead reads the **aim regardless of the beam's lit state** — a tile shift on beam toggle would read as a jump. (4) Predicate order: the inner-box clamp applies to the final pose, while lag/pan cuts read the unclamped follow term. Also: `T_PAN` is 0.10 s (6 / 15 / 3 frames at 60 / 144 / 30 fps) so the solver's predicates are frame-rate independent (written in seconds; the pose itself is bounded to within 1 base px across fps, D.6); the inner box is frame-relative (0.30 × field); Y-sort ties on an equal row break by layer order (tile layers before free items); *(superseded 2026-10-27 — design review: the free-item tie-break is now the class rank and stable entity ID of PR-5, never `x`)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

The extra width shows honest void in every dark state; the extra lit floor appears mainly in the stable home-ship state where there is no threat; there is no competitive stake (anti-pillar); and a third of the screen black at 1600×900 is the worse experience. > **Decided (orchestrator, consistency check 2026-10-26) — zoom-in vs the inner-box invariant (C7):** the look-ahead bound scales with the visible field, `L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX × field_h / 360` (72 → 54 px at the 270-row field of k = 4 at 1080p, 43.2 px at the 216-row field of k = 5 *(figures re-run 2026-10-26 — consistency check)*), so `v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX_eff ≤ 0.30·field_h` holds at every ladder step and running is never clamped by zoom; Section G's invariant is asserted at every reachable `field_h`, not only the default. Registry `camera_lookahead` and `speed_ceiling` carry the scaling. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check: with the Player Controller's `v_max` = 180 px/s the steady-state lag `v_max·τ_follow` = 32.4 px does not shrink with the field, so scaling `L_MAX` alone fails at every zoom-in step — 32.4 + 54 = 86.4 > 81 at 270 rows. The decision is therefore carried as "the solver's length parameters scale by `s = field_h / 360`": `τ_follow_eff`, `L_MAX_eff`, `L_SLEW_MAX_eff`, `LAG_CUT_eff` and `JUMP_CUT_eff` all scale, the pan ceiling `1.25·v_max` does not (it can never sit below `v_max`), and the invariant then holds at every field iff it holds at 360 — 24.3 + 54 = 78.3 ≤ 81 at 270; 64.8 + 144 = 208.8 ≤ 216 at 720; 36 + 80 = 116 ≤ 120 and 72 + 160 = 232 ≤ 240 at the Deck's 400 / 800. D.6, D.7, D.10 and Section G carry it.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `τ_follow_eff` scales by `min(1, s)`, not `s` — scaling τ up at `s > 1` made the frame keep drifting for 1.6 s after stopping at 1× on 1080p and 3.2 s on 2160p, against Game Feel "Stillness", and put `τ_eff` on 1600×900 `expand` (`s` = 1.25) outside its safe range; the other length parameters (`L_MAX`, `L_SLEW_MAX`, `LAG_CUT`, `JUMP_CUT`) still scale by `s`. The invariant becomes `0.30·field_h > v_max·τ·min(1, s) + L_MAX·s`, which is the unchanged scale-free check for `s ≤ 1` and reads `36·s > 32.4` for `s > 1` (true for all `s > 0.9`); re-run: 720: 32.4 + 144 = 176.4 ≤ 216; Deck 400: 32.4 + 80 = 112.4 ≤ 120; Deck 800: 32.4 + 160 = 192.4 ≤ 240.

**Camera states** (the `CameraSolver`'s state machine; every transition is a player input, a kernel state change or a solver rule — never world state, C1). **The camera's state is three independent fields, not one enum** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: **follow** ∈ {`FOLLOWING`, `CLAMPED`} (`CLAMPED` if either axis is clamped, driven only by the limits rect and the unclamped pose), **zoom** ∈ {default, `ZOOMED`} (`k_z ≠ k_base`, driven only by presses and `RESCALING`), and **hold** ∈ {live, `HELD`, `CUT`} (driven only by kernel and pipeline state and the cut rules). The rows below name the common combinations; every combination is legal and the transitions are independent: a zoom step changes only the zoom field (and is a `RESCALING` frame that re-derives the field, rescales the solver state per D.6 and re-evaluates the clamp, so a step can move `FOLLOWING` to `CLAMPED` and back); a `CUT` clears the smoothing history and the jolt but never the zoom field (except the VS-A re-wake) and never the follow field's rect; `HELD` freezes the pose without clearing zoom or clamp, and `PAUSED_FROZEN → PAUSED` resumes to live with no `CUT`; `LOADING` holds, and `RUNNING` cuts. Missing transitions made explicit: `ZOOMED` + `CLAMPED` is legal; a zoom press while `HELD` is discarded (Edge Cases); a rebase (`BODY_TRANSFER` with `frame_delta_px`) is a live-to-live transition that shifts state and clears nothing.

# TRs: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (pxl)

Source: design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-pxl-001 | The world is a 640x360 base-px logical canvas drawn at integer scale k = floor(min(W/640, H/360)) from window pixel size (never DPI; content_scale_factor 1.0), with minimum window 1280x720 so k >= 2, and no world node is ever drawn at a non-integer scale. | Rendering | PR-1, BASE_RESOLUTION, MIN_WINDOW |
| TR-pxl-002 | World content renders in its own SubViewport inside a SubViewportContainer (layer 0); HUD (layer 2), chart table/menus (layer 3), transit-hold quad (layer 1) and debug overlay (layer 4, dev only) are CanvasLayers above it that receive no world light, glow, ambient, occlusion, Filter pass or camera jolt. | Rendering | PR-3 layer model, HR-1/HR-13 |
| TR-pxl-003 | A single pipeline-root node is the only writer of SubViewport.size, size_2d_override, camera limits rect and the only caller of HudLayout; any window/mode/size change fires one RESCALING frame that re-derives k, H, logical size, letterbox, limits and world_to_hud. | Core | PR-2 Fullscreen, States RESCALING |
| TR-pxl-004 | Nearest filtering must be set in three places (project default_texture_filter=0, world SubViewport canvas_item_default_texture_filter=0, SubViewportContainer.texture_filter=TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST=1) and mipmaps are off on drawn sheets; SubViewport.size and TileSet.tile_size (48x48) are set explicitly. | Rendering | PR-3(f)(g), PR-4 rule 1 |

- Pipeline root node: sole writer of SubViewport.size, size_2d_override, camera limits rect, HudLayout caller, SubViewportContainer ShaderMaterial slot; startup assertion; RESCALING handling.

- Camera states (3 independent fields): FOLLOWING/CLAMPED, default/ZOOMED, live/HELD/CUT.
- CameraSolver (pure RefCounted `solve(input, state, params) -> pose`); camera host node writing world viewport `canvas_transform` in `frame_pre_draw`.
- `present_time` (render-rate clock, frozen in PAUSED).
- `world_to_hud(pos)`; `mouse_to_world_view(cursor)`; `mouse_to_world_aim(cursor, p)`; published `f_q`, `picture_centre`, `k_z`, picture rect, `k`, `k_base`, `H`.
- Z-band table (Floor, Floor marks, Y-sort, Wall caps, Dust) and sort key `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`; light-mask bits; `TILE_PX` 48; `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24.
- Layer model: World SubViewport, layer 1 transit hold, layer 2 Suit/HUD, layer 3 chart table/menus, layer 4 debug.
- `RENDER_MODE` {A, B}; `filter_route` slot (NOT_USED at MVP, PER_ELEMENT).
- Jolt API / berth Settle (default 0 at MVP; `JOLT_MAX`/`JOLT_PX`, `BERTH_SETTLE_PX`).
- Registry names: `BASE_RESOLUTION`, `MIN_WINDOW`, `TILE_PX`, `HUD_MIN_SCALE`, `FOLLOW_TAU`, `INNER_BOX_FRAC`, `LOOKAHEAD_PX`/`camera_lookahead`, `camera_follow`, `speed_ceiling`, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`, `flash_count`, `flash_governor`, `safe_margin` (HUD formula), `bottom_row_fit`, `RIM_FRINGE_PX`, `ZOOM_MIN_K`, `LAG_CUT`, `JUMP_CUT`, `L_SLEW_MAX`.
- Diagnostics: `diag.zoom_step_rate_limited`, `diag.zoom_step_refused`, `diag.inner_box_engaged`, per-viewport draw counts, camera state, driver name.
- Settings hooks (PR-14): display mode, resolution, integer world scale, HUD scale, reading-face scale, aspect keep/expand, frame cap, V-sync, reduced motion, reduce flashing, look-ahead strength.
- Test dir: tests/unit/render/.

## Consumes

- Command & Simulation Layer: PRESENTATION subscription (CR-10/CR-11), read views with previous/current, `tick_alpha` (clamped at 1), kernel states RUNNING/PAUSED/LOADING/SAVING, control plane for pause, CR-7 binding table, P5 notifications, `post_restore`.
- Player Controller & Input: local avatar (follow target), local raw beam aim, `loco_state`/movement octant, `AIM_ORIGIN`, `zoom_in`/`zoom_out` edge inputs, V_WALK/V_RUN (v_max).
- Ship Body & Interior Physics: body transforms, `BODY_TRANSFER` with `frame_delta_px`, `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT`, avatar body ID, loaded rect via PROJECTOR.
- Ship Section & Layout Data Model: namespace-tagged `entity_id`, door/doorway `area`, limits rect, sprite objects.
- Modular Ship Assembly: weld/detach notifications.
- Web Map & Transit: `pod_hop` Applied, `web.view.destination_ready`, `web.view.transit_state`, `BERTHED`, exterior-leg flag.
- Save/Load: `LOADING -> RUNNING`, `restore_reason`.
- 2D Lighting & Occlusion: lights/occluders in layer 0, ambient slot, per-light analytic flash clamp via modifier contract.
- Perception Filter: shader params, per-element materials, truth/corruptible tag contract.
- HUD & Suit Layer: layout function (`HudLayout`), safe margin, `bottom_row_fit`.
- Settings & Input Rebinding / Accessibility Settings: reduced motion, reduce flashing, scale settings.
- Chart Table: `D_L3` draw counts; Interaction System: prompt anchor requests; In-World Instruments, Horror Entities, Failure & Trail, Attention, Derelict Authoring, Emitter State, Suit & Equipment (sprites/bands/anchors); Debug Overlay (toggles).
- Art bible 8.1-8.4, 7.0 (constraints); Adaptive Audio (independence constraint only).

## Engine risk

- SubViewport / SubViewportContainer (stretch, stretch_shrink, size, size_2d_override, size_2d_override_stretch, render_target_update_mode UPDATE_ONCE/DISABLED): MEDIUM-HIGH. Wiring is NOT SOURCEABLE, spike step 11; treat as HIGH.
- Window content scale (canvas_items, integer scale_mode, Window.min_size, get_final_transform, size_changed/dpi_changed, MODE_FULLSCREEN vs EXCLUSIVE): MEDIUM (integer scale mode and Window APIs; unverified under 4.5-4.7 DPI behaviour).
- Viewport.get_mouse_position() unit under stretch and the 4.7 DEVICE_ID_MOUSE/KEYBOARD change: HIGH.
- Camera2D (process_callback IDLE, limit_*, position_smoothing, force_update_scroll, direct canvas_transform write from RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw): LOW for Camera2D, HIGH for frame_pre_draw ordering vs process_priority (unverified, 4.5+ behaviour).
- Parallax2D (replacement for ParallaxBackground): MEDIUM (4.3/4.4 era); host-driven fallback planned.
- Y-sort (y_sort_enabled, TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin, equal-row tree-order tie behaviour, z_index bands, Light2D range_z): LOW-MEDIUM; tie stability [UNV].
- snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel / snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel and their interaction with pass B: MEDIUM (unverified).
- Forward+ renderer, use_hdr_2d, use_debanding, 4.7 HDR output flag (key name NOT SOURCEABLE), 4.6 reworked glow (before tonemapping), D3D12 default on Windows 4.6+: HIGH.
- Light2D/PointLight2D/LightOccluder2D (light size_limit, shadows, mask bits): MEDIUM (cost shared with Lighting).
- 4.7 draw_line no feather/antialias change: HIGH.
- Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME) for per-viewport counts: LOW-MEDIUM.
- physics/common/physics_interpolation, physics_jitter_fix, max_physics_steps_per_frame, delta_smoothing, SceneTree.paused: LOW (4.6 Jolt default may affect physics tick relations).
- V-sync modes (VSYNC_MAILBOX, ADAPTIVE) and Vulkan vs D3D12 driver: HIGH.
- gui_snap_controls_to_pixels, CanvasLayer.scale, Control anchors/font rasterisation at final screen size: LOW.
- TileMapLayer and TileSet.tile_size (48): MEDIUM (TileMapLayer introduced 4.3).
- gdUnit4 headless project.godot parse test: LOW.

|---|---|---|---|

| TR-pxl-002 | World content renders in its own SubViewport inside a SubViewportContainer (layer 0); HUD (layer 2), chart table/menus (layer 3), transit-hold quad (layer 1) and debug overlay (layer 4, dev only) are CanvasLayers above it that receive no world light, glow, ambient, occlusion, Filter pass or camera jolt. | Rendering | PR-3 layer model, HR-1/HR-13 |
| TR-pxl-003 | A single pipeline-root node is the only writer of SubViewport.size, size_2d_override, camera limits rect and the only caller of HudLayout; any window/mode/size change fires one RESCALING frame that re-derives k, H, logical size, letterbox, limits and world_to_hud. | Core | PR-2 Fullscreen, States RESCALING |
